"1a71d282-d54a-40b3-a61a-1ef75935d6fd", "sha256": "374cfc2d089fa33b66a66c335afad73b3d23139d2e07fe4d6a7a67148762be00", "text": "## Decision

**Saldo is STRONGLY SUPPORTED as a calendar-year cumulative reported accounting amount for both resources.** A separate, guarded Automobile/Nacional transformation is justified by official accounting and publication evidence. It produces monthly changes in those reported amounts, including adjustments. Calling these pure monthly cash payments, earned premiums or accident-month losses is not justified.

The confidence is deliberately below CONFIRMED: CNBS has not supplied a field-specific CKAN dictionary or the extraction formula connecting Saldo to accounting accounts. The revised account manual inspected is dated January 2023; an unchanged extraction/accounting convention throughout 2018–2022 is not directly established. **Automobile is not ready for point-in-time historical replay**, because actual availability dates, historical revision vintages, exact account scope and the causes of negative increments remain unresolved.

## Separate derivation and safeguards

The policy is versioned in [config/cnbs_semantics.json](../../config/cnbs_semantics.json). Derivation requires CONFIRMED or STRONGLY SUPPORTED official temporal evidence and is restricted to exact `Seguros Generales` / `Vehículos Automotores` / currency `1` / `Nacional`, separately for each resource.

- January: `saldo_monthly_derived = saldo_reported`; previous December is never subtracted.
- February–December: subtract the exact prior calendar month end under the same `(resource, institution_code, parent_line, line, currency_code)`.
- Original raw files and original processed cumulative `saldo` remain unchanged. New files preserve those fields and add `saldo_reported`, `saldo_monthly_derived`, `saldo_derivation_status`, review flags and prior-value provenance.
- Invalid dates/amounts, non-month-end dates, duplicate/ambiguous keys, changed currency labels and missing prior months produce blank derived values with explicit blocked status. Selected rows are retained; outside-scope exclusion counts are explicit.
- Negative increments are retained and flagged, never clipped. Same-code institution-name changes are flagged; different codes, parent/line labels and currencies are never bridged. A code/name transition is not proof of legal continuity.
- An optional earlier raw baseline compares same-key amount/label changes and flags affected current/next-month differences. Added/deleted or ambiguous keys are separately reported. A December revision never contaminates January derivation. Snapshot differences do not establish an economic cause or original availability date.

`derived_*` means arithmetic was possible under this evidence policy, not that every amount is fully validated. `_review` requires documented treatment in retrospective evaluation and further investigation before economic interpretation. `blocked_*` has no monthly amount and must not be silently filtered or filled.
"}, {"id": "knowledge:replay", "document_id": "4d4ce8cb-eb3f-435f-a56a-a31e5e211b6a", "sha256": "d777b94850fb29ccdb660984f6ddfafd13ab49e9f0c4c2cf5257a880d328ee92", "text": "## C. Revisions and vintages

CNBS warns that figures may be revised after publication. The archived [publication portal](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/publication_portal.html), [evidence manifest](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/evidence_manifest.json) and [source registry](../reports/data-profile/cnbs_semantics_sources.json) preserve this evidence and retrieval provenance.

The current snapshot may contain later corrections or reclassifications to historical periods. There is only one distinct retained raw amount vintage per resource. Its content-addressed copy preserves the same bytes; it is not a second historical vintage. Distinct earlier raw vintages are not currently available in the repository.

The optional `--baseline-raw-dir` comparison can identify changes against a supplied earlier snapshot. It cannot retrieve missing vintages or establish original public availability dates. Publication discrepancies and negative monthly differences do not, by themselves, prove particular row revisions or their causes.

## Conservative reporting lag assumption

For retrospective evaluation, Actuarial Signal Radar applies a conservative two-month reporting lag. A month-end observation is considered available to the detection system on the first day of the third following calendar month. This assumption prevents the backtest from using unrealistically recent information and does not represent a confirmed CNBS publication schedule.

CNBS reporting periods are monthly. Exact historical public release dates have not been reconstructed, and current CKAN metadata is insufficient for strict point-in-time reconstruction. For the hackathon MVP, this deterministic calendar rule supplies simulated availability:

```text
availability_date = first day of the third calendar month following report_date
For evaluation date T: only records with availability_date <= T may be used.
```

| report_date | Simulated availability_date |
|---|---|
| 2020-01-31 | 2020-04-01 |
| 2021-02-28 | 2021-05-01 |
| 2020-02-29 | 2020-05-01 |
| 2020-03-31 | 2020-06-01 |
| 2020-04-30 | 2020-07-01 |
| 2020-05-31 | 2020-08-01 |
| 2020-06-30 | 2020-09-01 |
| 2021-12-31 | 2022-03-01 |

January data are unavailable on 2020-03-15 and become eligible on 2020-04-01, inclusively. Use calendar-month arithmetic, never `report_date + 60 days`. The phrase "60-day conservative reporting assumption" is shorthand only; elapsed days vary under the exact calendar rule. Prefer "conservative two-month reporting lag". Never claim "CNBS publishes exactly 60 days later".

The existing 33-day observation remains historical evidence, not the source of an exact lag estimate. Under this modeling assumption, 2026-08-31 becomes eligible on 2026-11-01 even though the snapshot proves it was already publicly available by 2026-10-03. Conservatism relative to report_date does not guarantee the assumed date is later than every actual historical release.

The pure helper [`preprocessing.availability.availability_date`](../actuarial-engine/preprocessing/availability.py) accepts a report-date string using the existing ISO parser and returns an ISO date string. It rejects invalid/non-month-end dates, performs no I/O, and is reused by the Phase 2 statistical replay engine. The derivation pipeline remains unchanged. Evaluation applies the inclusive eligibility filter before using observations. Timing for a derived increment also requires its source inputs to be eligible; the consecutive prior month precedes the current month under this monotone rule.

This changes the evaluation design to **LAGGED RETROSPECTIVE BACKTEST**. Availability is simulated; historical release dates and corresponding vintages remain unverified. This is distinct from verified lagged point-in-time replay and does not create strict point-in-time validity.

## E. Current acceptable evaluation design

Phase 2 implements a **lagged retrospective backtest** with the conservative two-month reporting lag using the fixed 2026-10-03 snapshot. Readiness is methodological permission to begin, not evidence that a backtest has already run or that a signal is valid.

Requirements enforced by the implementation:

1. Record the input snapshot date, hashes, scope and derivation policy with each evaluation result. Future downloads require a separately identified evaluation version.
2. At evaluation date `T`, first restrict all usable observations to `availability_date <= T`; `report_date` alone never grants eligibility. Process eligible monthly observations chronologically. Fit baselines, transformations and thresholds using only earlier reporting periods; evaluate the next period before updating. This prevents future-period leakage within the chosen snapshot, but cannot eliminate historical revision leakage.
3. Keep Primas and Siniestros separate and preserve institution codes. Define and disclose a cohort policy; selecting the ten complete institutions using the full history introduces hindsight/survivorship selection that must be reported. Do not silently bridge ASSA codes `0616` and `0618`.
4. Keep blocked monthly values missing, retain negatives and review flags, and document how flagged observations affect fitting and evaluation. Never silently fill blocked rows or clip negatives. Scope conclusions to reported accounting increments.
5. Distinguish reporting period from simulated availability date on the time axis. Without availability evidence, do not claim calendar-date alert delivery, real-time lead time or exactly what an insurer knew then. Do not treat the 33-day bound as a verified schedule.
6. Disclose the unknown release dates, possible revisions, cohort selection and unresolved account scope alongside results. No ground-truth anomaly labels or detection performance are established by this methodology.

```text
robust_z_t = 0.6745 * (x_t - median_past) / MAD_past
expected_lower/upper = median_past +/- alert_threshold * MAD_past / 0.6745
```

Default WATCH = 2.5 and ALERT = 3.5. The modified-z formula and 3.5 potential-outlier guideline follow [NIST's outlier discussion](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda35h.htm). WATCH = 2.5 is a disclosed exploratory intermediate threshold, not an empirical optimum. The [NIST MAD definition](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/mad.htm) supports the normal-reference scaling; it does not establish normality of these accounting increments.

## Signal and status policy

Each method/window emits its own score and decision; there is no black-box composite. Scores across methods have different meanings and are not directly comparable confidence measures.

- NORMAL: valid score with magnitude below WATCH.
- WATCH: magnitude at/above WATCH but below ALERT.
- ALERT: magnitude at/above ALERT, or at least three consecutive same-direction WATCH-or-stronger observations (configurable persistence_observations).
- Blank signal: not evaluated, with explicit evaluation_status such as insufficient_history, insufficient_history_gap, zero_variance, zero_mad, excluded_blocked, or excluded_invalid_value. It is never presented as NORMAL.

Direction change, normal observation, excluded row or calendar gap breaks persistence. Missing/blocked observations clear EWMA and CUSUM state, while valid older rows remain available only within the calendar window. No interpolation, zero filling, clipping or implicit institution bridging occurs. Numeric reasons include score, thresholds and consecutive count; source values, baseline statistics and dates are available in the same CSV row. Standard deviation and MAD zero are explicitly unscored even if the new value differs dramatically. Near-zero nonzero scales can yield extreme scores and warrant review.

## Interpretation boundary

This phase explores statistical deviations, not cause, prediction of disasters, strict point-in-time performance or validated actuarial loss-ratio monitoring. There are no independently adjudicated anomaly labels, accuracy estimates or operationally calibrated alert rates. Seasonality, inflation, trend, accounting adjustments, currency interpretation within the established scope and market composition can affect apparent signals. Many method/window/series comparisons create multiple-testing concerns. Nonstationarity and sample size limit classical control-chart interpretation. Phase 3 should review stable signals, seasonal/cohort sensitivity and quality context without choosing the most prolific flagger.
"}, {"id": "knowledge:expected_behavior", "document_id": "4838d01d-c52f-4f00-89e4-37598e7fe86d", "sha256": "ab8012ded85188d2f134e970fa35af7e1f0598afec433baa931eb4a10452f70f", "text": "## Raw, expected and residual views

Raw values are the existing guarded monthly accounting increments, not newly derived amounts. Phase 2 and its artifacts remain intact. Phase 3 provides three parallel views using the same detector implementations:

1. Raw monthly amount (or claims_to_premiums_ratio).
2. Trend-only residual: observed minus trailing trend.
3. Seasonally adjusted residual: observed minus (trailing trend plus prior month-of-year effect).

The third view is the primary anomaly interpretation layer. Raw values/signals remain essential context for amount, auditability and behavior that adjustment might mask. Expected values are historical model estimates, not contractual forecasts, causal explanations or validated actuarial expectations. Neither the raw ratio nor its expected value is an actuarial loss ratio.

## Economic materiality

Materiality is separate from statistical unusualness. Signed absolute_deviation equals observed minus expected; absolute_deviation_magnitude is its magnitude. For premium/claim amounts, absolute_deviation_lempiras reports the signed Lempira amount, consistent with the existing Nacional unit interpretation. Ratio deviations are ratio points and are never labeled Lempiras.

No defensible capital/budget thresholds have been established. Therefore classifications are **exploratory historical-impact bands**, fitted separately per series using only prior available full-model residual magnitudes from the last 36 calendar months, with at least 12 observations:

- LOW: magnitude below the prior empirical 75th percentile; zero is always LOW.
- MEDIUM: at/above the prior 75th percentile but below the prior 95th percentile.
- HIGH: at/above the prior 95th percentile.

Empirical quantiles use the nearest-rank order statistic, ceil(p*n). Insufficient materiality history yields no classification. Percentile thresholds and fit counts are emitted. Decision

**Saldo is STRONGLY SUPPORTED as a calendar-year cumulative reported accounting amount for both resources.** A separate, guarded Automobile/Nacional transformation is justified by official accounting and publication evidence. It produces monthly changes in those reported amounts, including adjustments. Calling these pure monthly cash payments, earned premiums or accident-month losses is not justified.

The confidence is deliberately below CONFIRMED: CNBS has not supplied a field-specific CKAN dictionary or the extraction formula connecting Saldo to accounting accounts. The revised account manual inspected is dated January 2023; an unchanged extraction/accounting convention throughout 2018–2022 is not directly established. **Automobile is not ready for point-in-time historical replay**, because actual availability dates, historical revision vintages, exact account scope and the causes of negative increments remain unresolved.

## Separate derivation and safeguards

The policy is versioned in [config/cnbs_semantics.json](../../config/cnbs_semantics.json). Derivation requires CONFIRMED or STRONGLY SUPPORTED official temporal evidence and is restricted to exact `Seguros Generales` / `Vehículos Automotores` / currency `1` / `Nacional`, separately for each resource.

- January: `saldo_monthly_derived = saldo_reported`; previous December is never subtracted.
- February–December: subtract the exact prior calendar month end under the same `(resource, institution_code, parent_line, line, currency_code)`.
- Original raw files and original processed cumulative `saldo` remain unchanged. New files preserve those fields and add `saldo_reported`, `saldo_monthly_derived`, `saldo_derivation_status`, review flags and prior-value provenance.
- Invalid dates/amounts, non-month-end dates, duplicate/ambiguous keys, changed currency labels and missing prior months produce blank derived values with explicit blocked status. Selected rows are retained; outside-scope exclusion counts are explicit.
- Negative increments are retained and flagged, never clipped. Same-code institution-name changes are flagged; different codes, parent/line labels and currencies are never bridged. A code/name transition is not proof of legal continuity.
- An optional earlier raw baseline compares same-key amount/label changes and flags affected current/next-month differences. Added/deleted or ambiguous keys are separately reported. A December revision never contaminates January derivation. Snapshot differences do not establish an economic cause or original availability date.

`derived_*` means arithmetic was possible under this evidence policy, not that every amount is fully validated. `_review` requires documented treatment in retrospective evaluation and further investigation before economic interpretation. `blocked_*` has no monthly amount and must not be silently filtered or filled.
"},{"id":"knowledge:replay","document_id":"4d4ce8cb-eb3f-435f-a56a-a31e5e211b6a","sha256":"d777b94850fb29ccdb660984f6ddfafd13ab49e9f0c4c2cf5257a880d328ee92","text":"## C. Revisions and vintages

CNBS warns that figures may be revised after publication. The archived [publication portal](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/publication_portal.html), [evidence manifest](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/evidence_manifest.json) and [source registry](../reports/data-profile/cnbs_semantics_sources.json) preserve this evidence and retrieval provenance.

The current snapshot may contain later corrections or reclassifications to historical periods. There is only one distinct retained raw amount vintage per resource. Its content-addressed copy preserves the same bytes; it is not a second historical vintage. Distinct earlier raw vintages are not currently available in the repository.

The optional `--baseline-raw-dir` comparison can identify changes against a supplied earlier snapshot. It cannot retrieve missing vintages or establish original public availability dates. Publication discrepancies and negative monthly differences do not, by themselves, prove particular row revisions or their causes.

## Conservative reporting lag assumption

For retrospective evaluation, Actuarial Signal Radar applies a conservative two-month reporting lag. A month-end observation is considered available to the detection system on the first day of the third following calendar month. This assumption prevents the backtest from using unrealistically recent information and does not represent a confirmed CNBS publication schedule.

CNBS reporting periods are monthly. Exact historical public release dates have not been reconstructed, and current CKAN metadata is insufficient for strict point-in-time reconstruction. For the hackathon MVP, this deterministic calendar rule supplies simulated availability:

```text
availability_date = first day of the third calendar month following report_date
For evaluation date T: only records with availability_date <= T may be used.
```

| report_date | Simulated availability_date |
|---|---|
| 2020-01-31 | 2020-04-01 |
| 2021-02-28 | 2021-05-01 |
| 2020-02-29 | 2020-05-01 |
| 2020-03-31 | 2020-06-01 |
| 2020-04-30 | 2020-07-01 |
| 2020-05-31 | 2020-08-01 |
| 2020-06-30 | 2020-09-01 |
| 2021-12-31 | 2022-03-01 |

January data are unavailable on 2020-03-15 and become eligible on 2020-04-01, inclusively. Use calendar-month arithmetic, never `report_date + 60 days`. The phrase "60-day conservative reporting assumption" is shorthand only; elapsed days vary under the exact calendar rule. Prefer "conservative two-month reporting lag". Never claim "CNBS publishes exactly 60 days later".

The existing 33-day observation remains historical evidence, not the source of an exact lag estimate. Under this modeling assumption, 2026-08-31 becomes eligible on 2026-11-01 even though the snapshot proves it was already publicly available by 2026-10-03. Conservatism relative to report_date does not guarantee the assumed date is later than every actual historical release.

The pure helper [`preprocessing.availability.availability_date`](../actuarial-engine/preprocessing/availability.py) accepts a report-date string using the existing ISO parser and returns an ISO date string. It rejects invalid/non-month-end dates, performs no I/O, and is reused by the Phase 2 statistical replay engine. The derivation pipeline remains unchanged. Evaluation applies the inclusive eligibility filter before using observations. Timing for a derived increment also requires its source inputs to be eligible; the consecutive prior month precedes the current month under this monotone rule.

This changes the evaluation design to **LAGGED RETROSPECTIVE BACKTEST**. Availability is simulated; historical release dates and corresponding vintages remain unverified. This is distinct from verified lagged point-in-time replay and does not create strict point-in-time validity.

## E. Current acceptable evaluation design

Phase 2 implements a **lagged retrospective backtest** with the conservative two-month reporting lag using the fixed 2026-10-03 snapshot. Readiness is methodological permission to begin, not evidence that a backtest has already run or that a signal is valid.

Requirements enforced by the implementation:

1. Record the input snapshot date, hashes, scope and derivation policy with each evaluation result. Future downloads require a separately identified evaluation version.
2. At evaluation date `T`, first restrict all usable observations to `availability_date <= T`; `report_date` alone never grants eligibility. Process eligible monthly observations chronologically. Fit baselines, transformations and thresholds using only earlier reporting periods; evaluate the next period before updating. This prevents future-period leakage within the chosen snapshot, but cannot eliminate historical revision leakage.
3. Keep Primas and Siniestros separate and preserve institution codes. Define and disclose a cohort policy; selecting the ten complete institutions using the full history introduces hindsight/survivorship selection that must be reported. Do not silently bridge ASSA codes `0616` and `0618`.
4. Keep blocked monthly values missing, retain negatives and review flags, and document how flagged observations affect fitting and evaluation. Never silently fill blocked rows or clip negatives. Scope conclusions to reported accounting increments.
5. Distinguish reporting period from simulated availability date on the time axis. Without availability evidence, do not claim calendar-date alert delivery, real-time lead time or exactly what an insurer knew then. Do not treat the 33-day bound as a verified schedule.
6. Disclose the unknown release dates, possible revisions, cohort selection and unresolved account scope alongside results. No ground-truth anomaly labels or detection performance are established by this methodology.

```text
robust_z_t = 0.6745 * (x_t - median_past) / MAD_past
expected_lower/upper = median_past +/- alert_threshold * MAD_past / 0.6745
```

Default WATCH = 2.5 and ALERT = 3.5. The modified-z formula and 3.5 potential-outlier guideline follow [NIST's outlier discussion](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda35h.htm). WATCH = 2.5 is a disclosed exploratory intermediate threshold, not an empirical optimum. The [NIST MAD definition](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/mad.htm) supports the normal-reference scaling; it does not establish normality of these accounting increments.

## Signal and status policy

Each method/window emits its own score and decision; there is no black-box composite. Scores across methods have different meanings and are not directly comparable confidence measures.

- NORMAL: valid score with magnitude below WATCH.
- WATCH: magnitude at/above WATCH but below ALERT.
- ALERT: magnitude at/above ALERT, or at least three consecutive same-direction WATCH-or-stronger observations (configurable persistence_observations).
- Blank signal: not evaluated, with explicit evaluation_status such as insufficient_history, insufficient_history_gap, zero_variance, zero_mad, excluded_blocked, or excluded_invalid_value. It is never presented as NORMAL.

Direction change, normal observation, excluded row or calendar gap breaks persistence. Missing/blocked observations clear EWMA and CUSUM state, while valid older rows remain available only within the calendar window. No interpolation, zero filling, clipping or implicit institution bridging occurs. Numeric reasons include score, thresholds and consecutive count; source values, baseline statistics and dates are available in the same CSV row. Standard deviation and MAD zero are explicitly unscored even if the new value differs dramatically. Near-zero nonzero scales can yield extreme scores and warrant review.

## Interpretation boundary

This phase explores statistical deviations, not cause, prediction of disasters, strict point-in-time performance or validated actuarial loss-ratio monitoring. There are no independently adjudicated anomaly labels, accuracy estimates or operationally calibrated alert rates. Seasonality, inflation, trend, accounting adjustments, currency interpretation within the established scope and market composition can affect apparent signals. Many method/window/series comparisons create multiple-testing concerns. Nonstationarity and sample size limit classical control-chart interpretation. Phase 3 should review stable signals, seasonal/cohort sensitivity and quality context without choosing the most prolific flagger.
"},{"id":"knowledge:expected_behavior","document_id":"4838d01d-c52f-4f00-89e4-37598e7fe86d","sha256":"ab8012ded85188d2f134e970fa35af7e1f0598afec433baa931eb4a10452f70f","text":"## Raw, expected and residual views

Raw values are the existing guarded monthly accounting increments, not newly derived amounts. Phase 2 and its artifacts remain intact. Phase 3 provides three parallel views using the same detector implementations:

1. Raw monthly amount (or claims_to_premiums_ratio).
2. Trend-only residual: observed minus trailing trend.
3. Seasonally adjusted residual: observed minus (trailing trend plus prior month-of-year effect).

The third view is the primary anomaly interpretation layer. Raw values/signals remain essential context for amount, auditability and behavior that adjustment might mask. Expected values are historical model estimates, not contractual forecasts, causal explanations or validated actuarial expectations. Neither the raw ratio nor its expected value is an actuarial loss ratio.

## Economic materiality

Materiality is separate from statistical unusualness. Signed absolute_deviation equals observed minus expected; absolute_deviation_magnitude is its magnitude. For premium/claim amounts, absolute_deviation_lempiras reports the signed Lempira amount, consistent with the existing Nacional unit interpretation. Ratio deviations are ratio points and are never labeled Lempiras.

No defensible capital/budget thresholds have been established. Therefore classifications are **exploratory historical-impact bands**, fitted separately per series using only prior available full-model residual magnitudes from the last 36 calendar months, with at least 12 observations:

- LOW: magnitude below the prior empirical 75th percentile; zero is always LOW.
- MEDIUM: at/above the prior 75th percentile but below the prior 95th percentile.
- HIGH: at/above the prior 95th percentile.

Empirical quantiles use the nearest-rank order statistic, ceil(p*n). Insufficient materiality history yields no classification. Percentile thresholds and fit counts are emitted. HIGH does not mean a validated actuarial/capital threshold, and per-institution HIGH bands are not comparable currency magnitudes. A very large robust z may have LOW materiality when the prior MAD is small. Claims ratio materiality is a relative ratio-impact rank, not money.

## Scientific boundary and next-stack recommendation

Use residual robust z / 12 months as the interpretable primary reference, standard z as a cross-check, CUSUM as a separate persistence channel, and raw values/signals plus materiality as context. Observed stability does not establish detection accuracy. Sensitivity results can weaken a signal's robustness without explaining its cause. Review cohort/adjustment/window agreement before escalating a retrospective early-warning signal.

Isolation Forest is **deferred** to preserve scientific clarity while deterministic modeling is assessed. No deep learning, AMD/ROCm/vLLM, Evolus, frontend or LLM explanations are implemented. Historical vintages/releases remain unavailable; exact accounting scope, revisions, seasonality drift, long warm-up, sparse same-month samples, changing institutions, near-zero scales and model misspecification remain limitations. There are no independently adjudicated anomalies, causal/disaster predictions, validated insurance loss ratios, strict point-in-time performance or real-time production claims.
"},{"id":"knowledge:case_selection","document_id":"4ef10a6d-e617-4638-8539-49e322e14ef5","sha256":"614e90b6ec953436ca2098cb536fe2dadac4f0c0ddf29ec8124411bf525a1bf8","text":"## Sensitivity labels

For saved cohort and negative-fit comparisons, require a scored alternative. Compare robust-score direction, signal level, and residual change:

```text
relative_residual_change = abs(alternative_residual - primary_residual)
                           / max(abs(primary_residual), 1e-12)
```

Same level and direction with change ≤25% yields **ROBUST** / **UNAFFECTED**. Same direction and alternative WATCH/ALERT otherwise yields **PARTIALLY_ROBUST** / **MODERATELY_SENSITIVE**. Remaining scored alternatives yield **SENSITIVE** / **HIGHLY_SENSITIVE**. The 25% tolerance is an explicit exploratory suitability convention, not a detector threshold; it avoids interpreting unchanged ALERT status alone as unchanged magnitude. “UNAFFECTED” means this operational label, not numerically identical fits. Exact alternate residuals and scores remain visible.

A missing/unscored comparison is **NOT_ASSESSED**, never ROBUST. Market roster sensitivity is **NOT_APPLICABLE** to independently modeled institution codes; this does not assess institution portfolio changes. If no negative-sensitive observation exists in the institution/metric history available through T, excluding such inputs would remove nothing: label UNAFFECTED by structural inspection, explicitly not by a new counterfactual run. Otherwise the unsaved institutional negative-fit comparison remains NOT_ASSESSED. Saved Phase 3 alternative fits cover markets only; institution window/fit coverage therefore remains incomplete.

The 24-month **trend** sensitivity is distinct from the unchanged 12-month residual **detector** reference. A scored alternative ALERT must retain corroboration for full sensitivity points; unscored history is not a vanished alert. The complete-history fixed cohort is hindsight-selected and remains a sensitivity only.

## Timing and interpretation

Scoring uses only source flags/history available through T and backward persistence. The T+1…T+3 observations are post-signal validation context, never input to suitability or original signals. Case selection itself is retrospective exploration of the current snapshot and is not prospective validation. Charts show up to 24 preceding and six following report months where saved data exist; later follow-up is shaded and the corresponding simulated availability dates appear on the top axis.

ALERT means substantial departure from modeled historical expectation deserving investigation. It does not establish fraud, a disaster, insolvency, cause or continued claims growth. Materiality bands remain exploratory; claims_to_premiums_ratio is not a validated actuarial loss ratio. Current-vintage revisions, unverified exact releases, incomplete institution counterfactuals and hindsight fixed-cohort selection limit interpretation. External investigation questions remain unanswered for a later phase.

Decision

**Saldo is STRONGLY SUPPORTED as a calendar-year cumulative reported accounting amount for both resources.** A separate, guarded Automobile/Nacional transformation is justified by official accounting and publication evidence. It produces monthly changes in those reported amounts, including adjustments. Calling these pure monthly cash payments, earned premiums or accident-month losses is not justified.

The confidence is deliberately below CONFIRMED: CNBS has not supplied a field-specific CKAN dictionary or the extraction formula connecting Saldo to accounting accounts. The revised account manual inspected is dated January 2023; an unchanged extraction/accounting convention throughout 2018–2022 is not directly established. **Automobile is not ready for point-in-time historical replay**, because actual availability dates, historical revision vintages, exact account scope and the causes of negative increments remain unresolved.

## Separate derivation and safeguards

The policy is versioned in [config/cnbs_semantics.json](../../config/cnbs_semantics.json). Derivation requires CONFIRMED or STRONGLY SUPPORTED official temporal evidence and is restricted to exact `Seguros Generales` / `Vehículos Automotores` / currency `1` / `Nacional`, separately for each resource.

- January: `saldo_monthly_derived = saldo_reported`; previous December is never subtracted.
- February–December: subtract the exact prior calendar month end under the same `(resource, institution_code, parent_line, line, currency_code)`.
- Original raw files and original processed cumulative `saldo` remain unchanged. New files preserve those fields and add `saldo_reported`, `saldo_monthly_derived`, `saldo_derivation_status`, review flags and prior-value provenance.
- Invalid dates/amounts, non-month-end dates, duplicate/ambiguous keys, changed currency labels and missing prior months produce blank derived values with explicit blocked status. Selected rows are retained; outside-scope exclusion counts are explicit.
- Negative increments are retained and flagged, never clipped. Same-code institution-name changes are flagged; different codes, parent/line labels and currencies are never bridged. A code/name transition is not proof of legal continuity.
- An optional earlier raw baseline compares same-key amount/label changes and flags affected current/next-month differences. Added/deleted or ambiguous keys are separately reported. A December revision never contaminates January derivation. Snapshot differences do not establish an economic cause or original availability date.

`derived_*` means arithmetic was possible under this evidence policy, not that every amount is fully validated. `_review` requires documented treatment in retrospective evaluation and further investigation before economic interpretation. `blocked_*` has no monthly amount and must not be silently filtered or filled.

CNBS warns that figures may be revised after publication. The archived [publication portal](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/publication_portal.html), [evidence manifest](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/evidence_manifest.json) and [source registry](../reports/data-profile/cnbs_semantics_sources.json) preserve this evidence and retrieval provenance.

The current snapshot may contain later corrections or reclassifications to historical periods. There is only one distinct retained raw amount vintage per resource. Its content-addressed copy preserves the same bytes; it is not a second historical vintage. Distinct earlier raw vintages are not currently available in the repository.

The optional `--baseline-raw-dir` comparison can identify changes against a supplied earlier snapshot. It cannot retrieve missing vintages or establish original public availability dates. Publication discrepancies and negative monthly differences do not, by themselves, prove particular row revisions or their causes.

## Conservative reporting lag assumption

For retrospective evaluation, Actuarial Signal Radar applies a conservative two-month reporting lag. A month-end observation is considered available to the detection system on the first day of the third following calendar month. This assumption prevents the backtest from using unrealistically recent information and does not represent a confirmed CNBS publication schedule.

CNBS reporting periods are monthly. Exact historical public release dates have not been reconstructed, and current CKAN metadata is insufficient for strict point-in-time reconstruction. For the hackathon MVP, this deterministic calendar rule supplies simulated availability:

```text
availability_date = first day of the third calendar month following report_date
For evaluation date T: only records with availability_date <= T may be used.
```

| report_date | Simulated availability_date |
|---|---|
| 2020-01-31 | 2020-04-01 |
| 2021-02-28 | 2021-05-01 |
| 2020-02-29 | 2020-05-01 |
| 2020-03-31 | 2020-06-01 |
| 2020-04-30 | 2020-07-01 |
| 2020-05-31 | 2020-08-01 |
| 2020-06-30 | 2020-09-01 |
| 2021-12-31 | 2022-03-01 |

January data are unavailable on 2020-03-15 and become eligible on 2020-04-01, inclusively. Use calendar-month arithmetic, never `report_date + 60 days`. The phrase "60-day conservative reporting assumption" is shorthand only; elapsed days vary under the exact calendar rule. Prefer "conservative two-month reporting lag". Never claim "CNBS publishes exactly 60 days later".

The existing 33-day observation remains historical evidence, not the source of an exact lag estimate. Under this modeling assumption, 2026-08-31 becomes eligible on 2026-11-01 even though the snapshot proves it was already publicly available by 2026-10-03. Conservatism relative to report_date does not guarantee the assumed date is later than every actual historical release.

The pure helper [`preprocessing.availability.availability_date`](../actuarial-engine/preprocessing/availability.py) accepts a report-date string using the existing ISO parser and returns an ISO date string. It rejects invalid/non-month-end dates, performs no I/O, and is reused by the Phase 2 statistical replay engine. The derivation pipeline remains unchanged. Evaluation applies the inclusive eligibility filter before using observations. Timing for a derived increment also requires its source inputs to be eligible; the consecutive prior month precedes the current month under this monotone rule.

This changes the evaluation design to **LAGGED RETROSPECTIVE BACKTEST**. Availability is simulated; historical release dates and corresponding vintages remain unverified. This is distinct from verified lagged point-in-time replay and does not create strict point-in-time validity.

## E. Current acceptable evaluation design

Phase 2 implements a **lagged retrospective backtest** with the conservative two-month reporting lag using the fixed 2026-10-03 snapshot. Readiness is methodological permission to begin, not evidence that a backtest has already run or that a signal is valid.

Requirements enforced by the implementation:

1. Record the input snapshot date, hashes, scope and derivation policy with each evaluation result. Future downloads require a separately identified evaluation version.
2. At evaluation date `T`, first restrict all usable observations to `availability_date <= T`; `report_date` alone never grants eligibility. Process eligible monthly observations chronologically. Fit baselines, transformations and thresholds using only earlier reporting periods; evaluate the next period before updating. This prevents future-period leakage within the chosen snapshot, but cannot eliminate historical revision leakage.
3. Keep Primas and Siniestros separate and preserve institution codes. Define and disclose a cohort policy; selecting the ten complete institutions using the full history introduces hindsight/survivorship selection that must be reported. Do not silently bridge ASSA codes `0616` and `0618`.
4. Keep blocked monthly values missing, retain negatives and review flags, and document how flagged observations affect fitting and evaluation. Never silently fill blocked rows or clip negatives. Scope conclusions to reported accounting increments.
5. Distinguish reporting period from simulated availability date on the time axis. Without availability evidence, do not claim calendar-date alert delivery, real-time lead time or exactly what an insurer knew then. Do not treat the 33-day bound as a verified schedule.
6. Disclose the unknown release dates, possible revisions, cohort selection and unresolved account scope alongside results. No ground-truth anomaly labels or detection performance are established by this methodology.
"},{"id":"knowledge:statistical","document_id":"d3beb26a-48a1-4a45-8dd0-409445c800a8","sha256":"ba45a3a8b3d11065c4f2affdffc4766532ecab88080f9df3ed566892c9b1f0dd","text":"## Robust z

```text
robust_z_t = 0.6745 * (x_t - median_past) / MAD_past
expected_lower/upper = median_past +/- alert_threshold * MAD_past / 0.6745
```

Default WATCH = 2.5 and ALERT = 3.5. The modified-z formula and 3.5 potential-outlier guideline follow [NIST's outlier discussion](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda35h.htm). WATCH = 2.5 is a disclosed exploratory intermediate threshold, not an empirical optimum. The [NIST MAD definition](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/mad.htm) supports the normal-reference scaling; it does not establish normality of these accounting increments.

## Signal and status policy

Each method/window emits its own score and decision; there is no black-box composite. Scores across methods have different meanings and are not directly comparable confidence measures.

- NORMAL: valid score with magnitude below WATCH.
- WATCH: magnitude at/above WATCH but below ALERT.
- ALERT: magnitude at/above ALERT, or at least three consecutive same-direction WATCH-or-stronger observations (configurable persistence_observations).
- Blank signal: not evaluated, with explicit evaluation_status such as insufficient_history, insufficient_history_gap, zero_variance, zero_mad, excluded_blocked, or excluded_invalid_value. It is never presented as NORMAL.

Direction change, normal observation, excluded row or calendar gap breaks persistence. Missing/blocked observations clear EWMA and CUSUM state, while valid older rows remain available only within the calendar window. No interpolation, zero filling, clipping or implicit institution bridging occurs. Numeric reasons include score, thresholds and consecutive count; source values, baseline statistics and dates are available in the same CSV row. Standard deviation and MAD zero are explicitly unscored even if the new value differs dramatically. Near-zero nonzero scales can yield extreme scores and warrant review.

## Interpretation boundary

This phase explores statistical deviations, not cause, prediction of disasters, strict point-in-time performance or validated actuarial loss-ratio monitoring. There are no independently adjudicated anomaly labels, accuracy estimates or operationally calibrated alert rates. Seasonality, inflation, trend, accounting adjustments, currency interpretation within the established scope and market composition can affect apparent signals. Many method/window/series comparisons create multiple-testing concerns. Nonstationarity and sample size limit classical control-chart interpretation. Phase 3 should review stable signals, seasonal/cohort sensitivity and quality context without choosing the most prolific flagger.
"},{"id":"knowledge:expected_behavior","document_id":"4838d01d-c52f-4f00-89e4-37598e7fe86d","sha256":"ab8012ded85188d2f134e970fa35af7e1f0598afec433baa931eb4a10452f70f","text":"## Raw, expected and residual views

Raw values are the existing guarded monthly accounting increments, not newly derived amounts. Phase 2 and its artifacts remain intact. Phase 3 provides three parallel views using the same detector implementations:

1. Raw monthly amount (or claims_to_premiums_ratio).
2. Trend-only residual: observed minus trailing trend.
3. Seasonally adjusted residual: observed minus (trailing trend plus prior month-of-year effect).

The third view is the primary anomaly interpretation layer. Raw values/signals remain essential context for amount, auditability and behavior that adjustment might mask. Expected values are historical model estimates, not contractual forecasts, causal explanations or validated actuarial expectations. Neither the raw ratio nor its expected value is an actuarial loss ratio.

## Economic materiality

Materiality is separate from statistical unusualness. Signed absolute_deviation equals observed minus expected; absolute_deviation_magnitude is its magnitude. For premium/claim amounts, absolute_deviation_lempiras reports the signed Lempira amount, consistent with the existing Nacional unit interpretation. Ratio deviations are ratio points and are never labeled Lempiras.

No defensible capital/budget thresholds have been established. Therefore classifications are **exploratory historical-impact bands**, fitted separately per series using only prior available full-model residual magnitudes from the last 36 calendar months, with at least 12 observations:

- LOW: magnitude below the prior empirical 75th percentile; zero is always LOW.
- MEDIUM: at/above the prior 75th percentile but below the prior 95th percentile.
- HIGH: at/above the prior 95th percentile.

Empirical quantiles use the nearest-rank order statistic, ceil(p*n). Insufficient materiality history yields no classification. Percentile thresholds and fit counts are emitted. HIGH does not mean a validated actuarial/capital threshold, and per-institution HIGH bands are not comparable currency magnitudes. A very large robust z may have LOW materiality when the prior MAD is small. Claims ratio materiality is a relative ratio-impact rank, not money.

## Scientific boundary and next-stack recommendation

Use residual robust z / 12 months as the interpretable primary reference, standard z as a cross-check, CUSUM as a separate persistence channel, and raw values/signals plus materiality as context. Observed stability does not establish detection accuracy. Sensitivity results can weaken a signal's robustness without explaining its cause. Review cohort/adjustment/window agreement before escalating a retrospective early-warning signal.

Isolation Forest is **deferred** to preserve scientific clarity while deterministic modeling is assessed. No deep learning, AMD/ROCm/vLLM, Evolus, frontend or LLM explanations are implemented. Historical vintages/releases remain unavailable; exact accounting scope, revisions, seasonality drift, long warm-up, sparse same-month samples, changing institutions, near-zero scales and model misspecification remain limitations. There are no independently adjudicated anomalies, causal/disaster predictions, validated insurance loss ratios, strict point-in-time performance or real-time production claims.
"},{"id":"knowledge:case_selection","document_id":"4ef10a6d-e617-4638-8539-49e322e14ef5","sha256":"614e90b6ec953436ca2098cb536fe2dadac4f0c0ddf29ec8124411bf525a1bf8","text":"## Sensitivity labels

For saved cohort and negative-fit comparisons, require a scored alternative. Compare robust-score direction, signal level, and residual change:

```text
relative_residual_change = abs(alternative_residual - primary_residual)
                           / max(abs(primary_residual), 1e-12)
```

Same level and direction with change ≤25% yields **ROBUST** / **UNAFFECTED**. Same direction and alternative WATCH/ALERT otherwise yields **PARTIALLY_ROBUST** / **MODERATELY_SENSITIVE**. Remaining scored alternatives yield **SENSITIVE** / **HIGHLY_SENSITIVE**. The 25% tolerance is an explicit exploratory suitability convention, not a detector threshold; it avoids interpreting unchanged ALERT status alone as unchanged magnitude. “UNAFFECTED” means this operational label, not numerically identical fits. Exact alternate residuals and scores remain visible.

A missing/unscored comparison is **NOT_ASSESSED**, never ROBUST. Market roster sensitivity is **NOT_APPLICABLE** to independently modeled institution codes; this does not assess institution portfolio changes. If no negative-sensitive observation exists in the institution/metric history available through T, excluding such inputs would remove nothing: label UNAFFECTED by structural inspection, explicitly not by a new counterfactual run. Otherwise the unsaved institutional negative-fit comparison remains NOT_ASSESSED. Saved Phase 3 alternative fits cover markets only; institution window/fit coverage therefore remains incomplete.

The 24-month **trend** sensitivity is distinct from the unchanged 12-month residual **detector** reference. A scored alternative ALERT must retain corroboration for full sensitivity points; unscored history is not a vanished alert. The complete-history fixed cohort is hindsight-selected and remains a sensitivity only.

## Timing and interpretation

Scoring uses only source flags/history available through T and backward persistence. The T+1…T+3 observations are post-signal validation context, never input to suitability or original signals. Case selection itself is retrospective exploration of the current snapshot and is not prospective validation. Charts show up to 24 preceding and six following report months where saved data exist; later follow-up is shaded and the corresponding simulated availability dates appear on the top axis.

ALERT means substantial departure from modeled historical expectation deserving investigation. It does not establish fraud, a disaster, insolvency, cause or continued claims growth. Materiality bands remain exploratory; claims_to_premiums_ratio is not a validated actuarial loss ratio. Current-vintage revisions, unverified exact releases, incomplete institution counterfactuals and hindsight fixed-cohort selection limit interpretation. External investigation questions remain unanswered for a later phase.
"},{"id":"knowledge:market_claims_2025_09","document_id":"16584e0b-60ff-459d-a55c-dcabcddfb32f","sha256":"7cf5e57a65a77239d9e6fe7f3d6883ab85cebf01db8ecf56b21c16d91af9ddd5","text":"## Observed vs expected

Decision

**Saldo is STRONGLY SUPPORTED as a calendar-year cumulative reported accounting amount for both resources.** A separate, guarded Automobile/Nacional transformation is justified by official accounting and publication evidence. It produces monthly changes in those reported amounts, including adjustments. Calling these pure monthly cash payments, earned premiums or accident-month losses is not justified.

The confidence is deliberately below CONFIRMED: CNBS has not supplied a field-specific CKAN dictionary or the extraction formula connecting Saldo to accounting accounts. The revised account manual inspected is dated January 2023; an unchanged extraction/accounting convention throughout 2018–2022 is not directly established. **Automobile is not ready for point-in-time historical replay**, because actual availability dates, historical revision vintages, exact account scope and the causes of negative increments remain unresolved.

## Separate derivation and safeguards

The policy is versioned in [config/cnbs_semantics.json](../../config/cnbs_semantics.json). Derivation requires CONFIRMED or STRONGLY SUPPORTED official temporal evidence and is restricted to exact `Seguros Generales` / `Vehículos Automotores` / currency `1` / `Nacional`, separately for each resource.

- January: `saldo_monthly_derived = saldo_reported`; previous December is never subtracted.
- February–December: subtract the exact prior calendar month end under the same `(resource, institution_code, parent_line, line, currency_code)`.
- Original raw files and original processed cumulative `saldo` remain unchanged. New files preserve those fields and add `saldo_reported`, `saldo_monthly_derived`, `saldo_derivation_status`, review flags and prior-value provenance.

- Negative increments are retained and flagged, never clipped. Same-code institution-name changes are flagged; different codes, parent/line labels and currencies are never bridged. A code/name transition is not proof of legal continuity.
- An optional earlier raw baseline compares same-key amount/label changes and flags affected current/next-month differences. Added/deleted or ambiguous keys are separately reported. A December revision never contaminates January derivation. Snapshot differences do not establish an economic cause or original availability date.

`derived_*` means arithmetic was possible under this evidence policy, not that every amount is fully validated. `_review` requires documented treatment in retrospective evaluation and further investigation before economic interpretation. `blocked_*` has no monthly amount and must not be silently filtered or filled.
"},{"id":"knowledge:replay","document_id":"4d4ce8cb-eb3f-435f-a56a-a31e5e211b6a","sha256":"d777b94850fb29ccdb660984f6ddfafd13ab49e9f0c4c2cf5257a880d328ee92","text":"## C. Revisions and vintages

CNBS warns that figures may be revised after publication. The archived [publication portal](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/publication_portal.html), [evidence manifest](../data/raw/cnbs_semantics/evidence_manifest.json) and [source registry](../reports/data-profile/cnbs_semantics_sources.json) preserve this evidence and retrieval provenance.

The current snapshot may contain later corrections or reclassifications to historical periods. There is only one distinct retained raw amount vintage per resource. Its content-addressed copy preserves the same bytes; it is not a second historical vintage. Distinct earlier raw vintages are not currently available in the repository.

The optional `--baseline-raw-dir` comparison can identify changes against a supplied earlier snapshot. It cannot retrieve missing vintages or establish original public availability dates. Publication discrepancies and negative monthly differences do not, by themselves, prove particular row revisions or their causes.

## Conservative reporting lag assumption

For retrospective evaluation, Actuarial Signal Radar applies a conservative two-month reporting lag. A month-end observation is considered available to the detection system on the first day of the third following calendar month. This assumption prevents the backtest from using unrealistically recent information and does not represent a confirmed CNBS publication schedule.

CNBS reporting periods are monthly. Exact historical public release dates have not been reconstructed, and current CKAN metadata is insufficient for strict point-in-time reconstruction. For the hackathon MVP, this deterministic calendar rule supplies simulated availability:

```text
availability_date = first day of the third calendar month following report_date
For evaluation date T: only records with availability_date <= T may be used.
```

| report_date | Simulated availability_date |
|---|---|
| 2020-01-31 | 2020-04-01 |
| 2021-02-28 | 2021-05-01 |
| 2020-02-29 | 2020-05-01 |
| 2020-03-31 | 2020-06-01 |
| 2020-04-30 | 2020-07-01 |
| 2020-05-31 | 2020-08-01 |
| 2020-06-30 | 2020-09-01 |
| 2021-12-31 | 2022-03-01 |

January data are unavailable on 2020-03-15 and become eligible on 2020-04-01, inclusively. Use calendar-month arithmetic, never `report_date + 60 days`. The phrase "60-day conservative reporting assumption" is shorthand only; elapsed days vary under the exact calendar rule. Prefer "conservative two-month reporting lag". Never claim "CNBS publishes exactly 60 days later".

The existing 33-day observation remains historical evidence, not the source of an exact lag estimate. Under this modeling assumption, 2026-08-31 becomes eligible on 2026-11-01 even though the snapshot proves it was already publicly available by 2026-10-03. Conservatism relative to report_date does not guarantee the assumed date is later than every actual historical release.

The pure helper [`preprocessing.availability.availability_date`](../actuarial-engine/preprocessing/availability.py) accepts a report-date string using the existing ISO parser and returns an ISO date string. It rejects invalid/non-month-end dates, performs no I/O, and is reused by the Phase 2 statistical replay engine. The derivation pipeline remains unchanged. Evaluation applies the inclusive eligibility filter before using observations. Timing for a derived increment also requires its source inputs to be eligible; the consecutive prior month precedes the current month under this monotone rule.

This changes the evaluation design to **LAGGED RETROSPECTIVE BACKTEST**. Availability is simulated; historical release dates and corresponding vintages remain unverified. This is distinct from verified lagged point-in-time replay and does not create strict point-in-time validity.

## E. Current acceptable evaluation design

Phase 2 implements a **lagged retrospective backtest** with the conservative two-month reporting lag using the fixed 2026-10-03 snapshot. Readiness is methodological permission to begin, not evidence that a backtest has already run or that a signal is valid.

Requirements enforced by the implementation:

1. Record the input snapshot date, hashes, scope and derivation policy with each evaluation result. Future downloads require a separately identified evaluation version.
2. At evaluation date `T`, first restrict all usable observations to `availability_date <= T`; `report_date` alone never grants eligibility. Process eligible monthly observations chronologically. Fit baselines, transformations and thresholds using only earlier reporting periods; evaluate the next period before updating. This prevents future-period leakage within the chosen snapshot, but cannot eliminate historical revision leakage.
3. Keep Primas and Siniestros separate and preserve institution codes. Define and disclose a cohort policy; selecting the ten complete institutions using the full history introduces hindsight/survivorship selection that must be reported. Do not silently bridge ASSA codes `0616` and `0618`.
4. Keep blocked monthly values missing, retain negatives and review flags, and document how flagged observations affect fitting and evaluation. Never silently fill blocked rows or clip negatives. Scope conclusions to reported accounting increments.
5. Distinguish reporting period from simulated availability date on the time axis. Without availability evidence, do not claim calendar-date alert delivery, real-time lead time or exactly what an insurer knew then. Do not treat the 33-day bound as a verified schedule.
6. Disclose the unknown release dates, possible revisions, cohort selection and unresolved account scope alongside results. No ground-truth anomaly labels or detection performance are established by this methodology.

```text
robust_z_t = 0.6745 * (x_t - median_past) / MAD_past
expected_lower/upper = median_past +/- alert_threshold * MAD_past / 0.6745
```

Default WATCH = 2.5 and ALERT = 3.5. The modified-z formula and 3.5 potential-outlier guideline follow [NIST's outlier discussion](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda35h.htm). WATCH = 2.5 is a disclosed exploratory intermediate threshold, not an empirical optimum. The [NIST MAD definition](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/mad.htm) supports the normal-reference scaling; it does not establish normality of these accounting increments.

## Signal and status policy

Each method/window emits its own score and decision; there is no black-box composite. Scores across methods have different meanings and are not directly comparable confidence measures.

- NORMAL: valid score with magnitude below WATCH.
- WATCH: magnitude at/above WATCH but below ALERT.
- ALERT: magnitude at/above ALERT, or at least three consecutive same-direction WATCH-or-stronger observations (configurable persistence_observations).
- Blank signal: not evaluated, with explicit evaluation_status such as insufficient_history, insufficient_history_gap, zero_variance, zero_mad, excluded_blocked, or excluded_invalid_value. It is never presented as NORMAL.

Direction change, normal observation, excluded row or calendar gap breaks persistence. Missing/blocked observations clear EWMA and CUSUM state, while valid older rows remain available only within the calendar window. No interpolation, zero filling, clipping or implicit institution bridging occurs. Numeric reasons include score, thresholds and consecutive count; source values, baseline statistics and dates are available in the same CSV row. Standard deviation and MAD zero are explicitly unscored even if the new value differs dramatically. Near-zero nonzero scales can yield extreme scores and warrant review.

## Interpretation boundary

This phase explores statistical deviations, not cause, prediction of disasters, strict point-in-time performance or validated actuarial loss-ratio monitoring. There are no independently adjudicated anomaly labels, accuracy estimates or operationally calibrated alert rates. Seasonality, inflation, trend, accounting adjustments, currency interpretation within the established scope and market composition can affect apparent signals. Many method/window/series comparisons create multiple-testing concerns. Nonstationarity and sample size limit classical control-chart interpretation. Phase 3 should review stable signals, seasonal/cohort sensitivity and quality context without choosing the most prolific flagger.
"},{"id":"knowledge:expected_behavior","document_id":"4838d01d-c52f-4f00-89e4-37598e7fe86d","sha256":"ab8012ded85188d2f134e970fa35af7e1f0598afec433baa931eb4a10452f70f","text":"## Raw, expected and residual views

Raw values are the existing guarded monthly accounting increments, not newly derived amounts. Phase 2 and its artifacts remain intact. Phase 3 provides three parallel views using the same detector implementations:

1. Raw monthly amount (or claims_to_premiums_ratio).
2. Trend-only residual: observed minus trailing trend.
3. Seasonally adjusted residual: observed minus (trailing trend plus prior month-of-year effect).

The third view is the primary anomaly interpretation layer. Raw values/signals remain essential context for amount, auditability and behavior that adjustment might mask. Expected values are historical model estimates, not contractual forecasts, causal explanations or validated actuarial expectations. Neither the raw ratio nor its expected value is an actuarial loss ratio.

## Economic materiality

Materiality is separate from statistical unusualness. Signed absolute_deviation equals observed minus expected; absolute_deviation_magnitude is its magnitude. For premium/claim amounts, absolute_deviation_lempiras reports the signed Lempira amount, consistent with the existing Nacional unit interpretation. Ratio deviations are ratio points and are never labeled Lempiras.

No defensible capital/budget thresholds have been established. Therefore classifications are **exploratory historical-impact bands**, fitted separately per series using only prior available full-model residual magnitudes from the last 36 calendar months, with at least 12 observations:

- LOW: magnitude below the prior empirical 75th percentile; zero is always LOW.
- MEDIUM: at/above the prior 75th percentile but below the prior 95th percentile.
- HIGH: at/above the prior 95th percentile.

Empirical quantiles use the nearest-rank order statistic, ceil(p*n). Insufficient materiality history yields no classification. Percentile thresholds and fit counts are emitted. HIGH does not mean a validated actuarial/capital threshold, and per-institution HIGH bands are not comparable currency magnitudes. A very large robust z may have LOW materiality when the prior MAD is small. Claims ratio materiality is a relative ratio-impact rank, not money.

## Scientific boundary and next-stack recommendation

Use residual robust z / 12 months as the interpretable primary reference, standard z as a cross-check, CUSUM as a separate persistence channel, and raw values/signals plus materiality as context. Observed stability does not establish detection accuracy. Sensitivity results can weaken a signal's robustness without explaining its cause. Review cohort/adjustment/window agreement before escalating a retrospective early-warning signal.

Isolation Forest is **deferred** to preserve scientific clarity while deterministic modeling is assessed. No deep learning, AMD/ROCm/vLLM, Evolus, frontend or LLM explanations are implemented. Historical vintages/releases remain unavailable; exact accounting scope, revisions, seasonality drift, long warm-up, sparse same-month samples, changing institutions, near-zero scales and model misspecification remain limitations. There are no independently adjudicated anomalies, causal/disaster predictions, validated insurance loss ratios, strict point-in-time performance or real-time production claims.
"},{"id":"knowledge:case_selection","document_id":"4ef10a6d-e617-4638-8539-49e322e14ef5","sha256":"614e90b6ec953436ca2098cb536fe2dadac4f0c0ddf29ec8124411bf525a1bf8","text":"## Sensitivity labels

For saved cohort and negative-fit comparisons, require a scored alternative. Compare robust-score direction, signal level, and residual change:

```text
relative_residual_change = abs(alternative_residual - primary_residual)
                           / max(abs(primary_residual), 1e-12)
```

Same level and direction with change ≤25% yields **ROBUST** / **UNAFFECTED**. Same direction and alternative WATCH/ALERT otherwise yields **PARTIALLY_ROBUST** / **MODERATELY_SENSITIVE**. Remaining scored alternatives yield **SENSITIVE** / **HIGHLY_SENSITIVE**. The 25% tolerance is an explicit exploratory suitability convention, not a detector threshold; it avoids interpreting unchanged ALERT status alone as unchanged magnitude. “UNAFFECTED” means this operational label, not numerically identical fits. Exact alternate residuals and scores remain visible.

A missing/unscored comparison is **NOT_ASSESSED**, never ROBUST. Market roster sensitivity is **NOT_APPLICABLE** to independently modeled institution codes; this does not assess institution portfolio changes. If no negative-sensitive observation exists in the institution/metric history available through T, excluding such inputs would remove nothing: label UNAFFECTED by structural inspection, explicitly not by a new counterfactual run. Otherwise the unsaved institutional negative-fit comparison remains NOT_ASSESSED. Saved Phase 3 alternative fits cover markets only; institution window/fit coverage therefore remains incomplete.

The 24-month **trend** sensitivity is distinct from the unchanged 12-month residual **detector** reference. A scored alternative ALERT must retain corroboration for full sensitivity points; unscored history is not a vanished alert. The complete-history fixed cohort is hindsight-selected and remains a sensitivity only.

## Timing and interpretation

Scoring uses only source flags/history available through T and backward persistence. The T+1…T+3 observations are post-signal validation context, never input to suitability or original signals. Case selection itself is retrospective exploration of the current snapshot and is not prospective validation. Charts show up to 24 preceding and six following report months where saved data exist; later follow-up is shaded and the corresponding simulated availability dates appear on the top axis.

ALERT means substantial departure from modeled historical expectation deserving investigation. It does not establish fraud, a disaster, insolvency, cause or continued claims growth. Materiality bands remain exploratory; claims_to_premiums_ratio is not a validated actuarial loss ratio. Current-vintage revisions, unverified exact releases, incomplete institution counterfactuals and hindsight fixed-cohort selection limit interpretation. External investigation questions remain unanswered for a later phase.
